sampling_model.design: For each analyst-selected \(s\), the assignment law is chosen from all outcome-independent probability distributions on \(\{0,1\}^{2J}\); after pair-preserving symmetrization it is represented by \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\).
sampling_model.units: The \(2J\) labelled units and all binary potential outcomes are fixed; only the partition into \(J\) pairs is observed before assignment, while armwise discordance is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: A binary assignment \(A\) is the only source of randomness, and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}=A_{jr}Y_{jr}(1)+(1-A_{jr})Y_{jr}(0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No marginal positivity restriction is imposed; zero-mass assignment and observation cells are handled by closed quadratic perspectives and explicit primal completions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no sampled nuisances. Nature chooses a fixed schedule in the sensitivity class \(\Theta_{J,s}\); risks, optimal procedures, and confidence sets are reported separately as \(s\) varies.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Given an assignment vector and an invariant estimator, uniform randomization over the permutation group is minimax under invariant states and a quasiconvex objective.
The mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes worst-case variance of difference in means over a structured conditional-mean class and may require randomization over several partitions.
For unrestricted binary potential outcomes, Bernoulli assignment with a nonlinear posterior-mean rule attains the all-procedure minimax risk, whose second-order term is governed by the Airy function.

For the unrestricted bounded-interval class, independent assignment and a nonlinear rule attain the all-estimator minimax value; the endpoint-supported least-favourable prior supplies the lower side needed to transfer that value and procedure to the present binary endpoint subclass.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Proposition 2 (same-value and procedure transfer by sandwich only)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: In a superpopulation stratified experiment constrained to treat half of every stratum, matched pairs formed by the prognostic index minimize the mean-squared error of difference in means.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: unmatched; the model and decision classes are non-nested

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For a fixed stratified design with unbiased uncorrelated group-CATE estimators, homoscedastic outcomes, and bounded group CATEs, Theorem 2.1 finds the lowest worst-case-MSE linear combination of those estimators.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: unmatched; the fixed-design linear-estimator problem and the present joint all-estimator design problem are non-nested

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The Gram--Schmidt Walk design controls a covariance-based balance--robustness trade-off and yields MSE and asymptotic inference guarantees for Horvitz--Thompson estimation.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, the minimax bound is attained if and only if inclusion indicators are pairwise independent.
Under within-pair coin flips, the worst compatible binary attributable-effect allocation is a single boundary corner and exact inversion needs logarithmically many binomial tails.
Exact binary ATE intervals under balanced Bernoulli or matched-pair assignment can be computed with \(O(\log n)\) randomization tests.
Exact conservative stratified binary ATE inference can be obtained by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over compatible potential-outcome tables.

body.tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-selected sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction yields an exact finite conic game, a polynomial-size rational kernel, and dual certificates for the entire invariant optimal-design correspondence; an exact \(J=2,s=1\) certificate rules out every paired--Bernoulli mixture. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while the leading term is flat on a measure-valued face at and above the threshold. The unresolved selection problem is now localized at \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\): the candidate hard-budget correction competes with the unrestricted \(J^{-4/3}\) Airy scale, but only an upper construction is presently available. At \(s=J\), the class is exactly the unrestricted binary class, while comparison with the larger bounded-interval class transfers the same value and procedure only by a two-sided sandwich.

project_justification.gap: Published minimax results cover unrestricted binary schedules, a larger unrestricted bounded-interval class, superpopulation matched-pair precision under half-treatment constraints, or linear shrinkage under a fixed stratified design. They do not solve the intermediate fixed-population class indexed by a latent armwise pair-discordance cap while jointly choosing every assignment law and every measurable estimator, and they do not characterize limits of exact finite minimizers on the flat first-order face. The superpopulation half-treatment and fixed-design linear-estimator comparators are non-nested with the present problem.
project_justification.niche: The latent discordance restriction breaks full unit exchangeability without pretending that unobserved potential-outcome similarity is pretreatment information. It creates a finite nontransitive observation experiment in which correlated assignment laws and nonlinear posterior-mean rules can be jointly optimal, with a critical hard-budget perturbation at \(s_J-J/2=O(J^{2/3})\).
project_justification.fill: For each selected \(s\), the project supplies the normalized orbit game, a matching least-favourable-prior dual, exact canonicality and uniqueness certificates, a strict noncanonical separation, a monotone risk frontier, the sharp first-order phase transition, its first-order design face, and exact randomization-test inversion. It additionally formulates, but does not solve, the residual \(J^{4/3}\)-scaled epi-limit and exact-minimizer contact problem.

body.related_work: Bai2023WhyRandomize supplies a symmetry template, and Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured minimax design may require randomization over several partitions; neither solves the present all-estimator hard-discordance game. SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 treats exactly the unrestricted binary class obtained here at \(s=J\), including Bernoulli assignment, a nonlinear posterior-mean rule, and an Airy second-order expansion. Hull2026BoundedOutcomes treats a larger bounded-interval class. The present binary endpoint is only its endpoint-valued subclass: Hull's uniform procedure bounds the binary minimax value from above, while Hull's endpoint-supported least-favourable prior supplies the reverse lower bound, so the same value and procedure transfer without class identity or experiment equivalence. Bai2022MatchedPairs studies a superpopulation stratified problem constrained to treat half of each stratum; deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage studies a fixed-design problem optimized only over linear combinations of group estimators. Those two problems are different from and non-nested with the present fixed-population joint design--all-estimator game. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 and AronowLopatto2026 inform assignment dependence under specified estimator or unbiasedness restrictions. Wilson2026MatchedBinary, Zhang2026FastBinaryCI, and LiSpertusStark2025 inform exact inversion, but their product or fixed-stratum mechanisms do not cover correlated noncanonical laws under a latent mismatch sensitivity class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected kernel has been checked by exact row normalization for every \((h,n)\) at \(J=2,3,4\), and exact rational inequalities certify the strict noncanonical separation only at \(J=2,s=1\). Other displayed finite risks and projected face diagnostics are numerical early-kill checks, not theorem contributions; in particular, the critical grids \(J=2,s=1\) and \(J=4,s=2\) do not establish a stable exact-selection law. The first-order van Trees arguments use smooth boundary-vanishing priors on finite positive-cell experiments and positive finite-\(J\) information regularization, but they control only the \(J^{-1}\) term. Writing \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\) shows that the candidate design correction \((2\overline m_J-1)\Delta_J/J^2\) meets an unrestricted \(J^{-4/3}\) Airy correction on the \(J^{2/3}\) budget scale. This correction is upper-bound evidence only. No matching lower expansion, boundary-uniform pair-orbit local experiment, epi-limit, convergence of minima, or exact-minimizer recovery theorem has been proved; finite \(\kappa\), the two infinite one-sided regimes, and fixed \(\rho>1/2\) must be analyzed separately.
body.honest_scope: The parameter \(s\) is an analyst-selected sensitivity index for latent both-arm discordance, not an observed or administratively verifiable quantity. Every risk, optimal face, asymptotic regime, and confidence set is conditional on the selected value or sequence. The finite orbit representation, endpoint reductions, rational noncanonical separation, first-order value, low-sensitivity concentration, high-sensitivity first-order envelope, and exact inversion are theorem obligations. At \(s=J\), the schedule class is exactly the unrestricted binary class of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026. It is only the endpoint-valued subclass of Hull2026BoundedOutcomes' bounded-interval class; equality of minimax values and transfer of the Bernoulli nonlinear procedure follow by the uniform-upper-bound and endpoint-prior lower-bound sandwich, not by class identity. For \(\rho\ge1/2\), exact finite minimizers may select a strict subset of the first-order face. The \(J^{4/3}\)-scaled candidate with hard-budget term \(\kappa(2\int m\,d\mu-1)\) is not yet a proved limit, and the exact contact set remains open in the finite-\(\kappa\), one-sided infinite-\(\kappa\), and fixed-supercritical regimes.
